correctness.rationale: Proof of iff: order-four apex survival expansion forces Q1=0; Q1=0 yields exact two-level evolution. Connected simple bicyclic graph with minimum degree two has either one degree-four root (figure-eight) or two degree-three roots (theta or barbell), by the handshaking excess 2. Degree-two rows force alternating phases along paths, giving parity-dependent far-end contributions. Theta endpoints yield the equilateral triple plus a real-part constraint, proving precisely two circles or four points; cycle roots give zero from even lobes or 2 Re(t) from odd lobes, proving exact barbell obstruction and eight assignments. Every parameter boundary in the theorem is covered. The bundled standalone test directly constructs 1,145 cones and checks moments through order 12, but finite tests are not relied on for infinity.

originality.rationale: The original content is the complete bicyclic minimum-degree-and-barbell-parity equivalence together with the theta parity-dependent two-circle versus four-point phase space and the exact eight assignments on odd–odd barbells. Frigerio–Paris establishes the row-sum criterion and covers even-degree graphs (hence figure-eights) and regular cubic graphs, but its inspected statements and proofs do not imply the new family classification without the new degree-two path and branch-root analysis. Later primary sources investigate endpoint transport and unit-gain products. These assessments compare mathematical implications, not just titles; remaining unlocated stronger-criterion risk is expressly recorded.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete solution, not a small arbitrary parameter computation, of optimal phase-only apex transport for every connected graph of cyclomatic number two. The sharp parity obstruction for an even barbell lobe despite minimum degree two and the continuous-to-discrete theta phase-space transition meaningfully inform network design and distinguish intrinsic topology from phase freedom. Known general and all-even-degree results are expressly credited; only the full classification and new phase constraints are advanced.
